x: AR1 (1990) fed into the UNFCCC of 1992. The Convention was adopted on 9 May 1992 in New York and opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992. Kyoto (1997), Paris (2015) and Montreal (1987) came later or deal with other issues.

Rentachintala in Palnadu is the hottest place in Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are wrong: South Asia's first Heat Action Plan was Ahmedabad's (2013), CRIDA is in Hyderabad and ICRISAT is at Patancheru, Hyderabad.
Lakshadweep is made up entirely of atoll reefs. The giant Pavona clavus (potato patch coral) colony was found there at Kadmat. Fringing, barrier and deep-sea cold-water reefs do not describe it.

CBDR-RC appears in Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration, Article 3.1 of the UNFCCC and Article 2.2 of the Paris Agreement ('in the light of different national circumstances'). The notes list no Article 10.5 of the Kyoto Protocol for it, so pair 4 is left out: '1, 2 and 3 only'.

The India-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism, signed in August 2025, is a bilateral cooperative approach under Article 6.2. Its Rules of Implementation were adopted in January 2026. Article 6.4 is the UN-run PACM, Article 9.1 covers finance from developed countries and Article 14 is the Global Stocktake.
The APPSC-GS 2024 key links Saraswathi of Malluvalasa (AP natural-farming practitioner) with 'Sustaina India 2025'. ⚠ Sources differ: one guide links her to COP28 instead, so check the official key.
All three are correct. CITES regulates international trade in endangered species, is known as the Washington Convention and was signed in 1973 (one source's 1963 is wrong).
